Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-10-15 14:00 UTC
Duration: 55m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nambiar (Head of ML - Velocity), Ethan Cole (CTO - Velocity), Rita Singh (Procurement), James Park (PM)
Shared links: deck: https://redwood.ai/s/vel-readout-deck, benchmark sheet: https://redwood.ai/s/vel-bench-2025, security pack: https://redwood.ai/s/vel-security-pack

Summary (auto): quick readout of POC results, agreement on pass/fail thresholds, and alignment on commercial next steps.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay everyone good, thanks for making time. We wanted to keep this tight, 45-ish minutes, we'll go through the numbers, Diego will cover the tuning we did, then open for questions and next steps.
[00:23] Priya Nambiar: Sounds good. Appreciate it. we've got a couple execs on the line so if we need to pause for clarifications, say so.
[00:31] Diego Alvarez: Great. I'll jump in right away with the benchmark summary. The sheet I shared - row "Week6-final" - contains the runs. Quick tl;dr: with prefix KV caching on and the 4-bit quant profile we recommended, average latency for our short chat intent set was 120ms median, 150ms 95th, cost about $0.95 per 1k tokens effective once caching hit-rate is applied.
[01:02] Ethan Cole: Sorry can you repeat the 95th? I heard 150ms 95th.
[01:07] Diego Alvarez: Yep 150ms 95th for the short intents (<=64 tokens). For the longer gen flows (>=256 tokens) 95th was about 380ms, but we see room for batching.
[01:25] Priya Nambiar: The key metric for us is not tail latency for long docs, it's the responsiveness on triage chat. So the short intents are the important ones.
[01:33] Maya Chen: Good, that's what we used for success criteria in the POC. Diego, can you briefly explain what changed between week 4 and week 6?
[01:42] Diego Alvarez: Sure. Week 4 we were running default fp16 on the larger model variant; we switched to 4-bit quant (we tested two quant profiles), and enabled prefix caching plus a lightweight KV cache with an LRU of 10k entries. Also we adjusted kernel selection to prefer tiled-attention for short sequences which dropped per-token overhead. The result was about 25-30% latency improvement and ~40% cost reduction on the short intent set.
[02:12] James Park: There were some hallucination cases in the hand-labeled eval set — did the quantization cause any WER/regression?
[02:18] Diego Alvarez: Good question. We ran the 5k human-labeled prompts and measured intent accuracy and a small set of safety regressions. Intent accuracy improved slightly (baseline 86.7% -> 88.3%); we did not see a statistically significant increase in factual hallucinations on the eval sample. There were a couple of edge cases with date normalization that we tagged.
[02:41] Priya Nambiar: Right, Priya again, the accuracy bump is nice but the edge date issues would be higher priority in our acceptance tests. Can y'all add a narrow prompt rule to catch date normalizations?
[02:52] Diego Alvarez: Absolutely, we already prototyped a small prompt post-filter that normalizes dates; I'll include that in the final run.
[03:01] Rita Singh: On procurement timeline — if we move to reserved capacity what's the minimum term?
[03:07] Maya Chen: Typical reserved contract is 12 months for the committed GPUs, with a 30-day termination window for add-ons. We can outline a pilot-to-reserve conversion clause in the SOW. We'll send a draft.
[03:18] Rita Singh: And pricing — the effective cost you quoted includes caching assumptions, right?
[03:23] Diego Alvarez: Correct. The $0.95 per 1k tokens reflects the observed cache hit rate of ~48% from the POC traffic. Without caching the same model would be roughly $1.60 per 1k tokens in our current price band.
[03:39] Ethan Cole: Are there any single points of failure in the hosted path? We're particularly sensitive to availability.
[03:45] Maya Chen: We recommend a failover plan — route to an alternate region or to a smaller-but-stable model variant for graceful degradation. Redwood Console supports automatic fallback by policy. Also we can discuss Dedicated capacity if you need more isolation/SLA.
[04:01] Ethan Cole: For compliance, SOC2 plus KMS for key management is a must. How deep are your audit logs?
[04:08] Diego Alvarez: We capture token-level metadata for cost and latency tracing, redacted-by-default content logs if you enable retention, and we integrate with customer KMS for encryption-at-rest. The security pack link has the SOC2 report excerpt and sample audit logs.
[04:25] Priya Nambiar: A quick nit — the transcript from last week's demo had some misreadings of K V cache as K V cash in the notes; just flagging because procurement was confused.
[04:33] Maya Chen: Noted, thanks. We sometimes get transcription noise, will correct the doc.
[04:39] James Park: On the technical accept criteria — can we restate them so everyone is aligned?
[04:44] Priya Nambiar: I'll say the pass criteria: (1) 95th <= 180ms for short intents on our 5k sample, (2) average intent accuracy >= 88% on the labeled set, (3) effective cost <= $1.20 per 1k tokens with the observed cache behavior, (4) no high-severity regression in safety checks.
[05:07] Diego Alvarez: We meet all four based on the final run; the safety regressions were low-sev and we have mitigations for the date normalization.
[05:13] Ethan Cole: That's promising. From an infra POV, we may want a private VPC deployment for traffic egress controls. Is that available in Redwood Private?
[05:22] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC peering and on-prem packages for regulated workloads. There's an added setup and licensing cadence for Private deployments — Diego can go into the checklist after this call if useful.
[05:34] Diego Alvarez: Quick notes: if you go Private we do a short on-site or remote network validation, key rotation steps for KMS, and we generally preserve the same rollback/fallback policies. It adds around 3-4 weeks to go-live depending on procurement.
[05:47] Rita Singh: Procurement will need the SOC2 and a sample DPA. We have a security questionnaire we need answered by 10/28.
[05:54] Maya Chen: We'll populate your questionnaire; Diego will own tech-specific Qs.
[06:00] Priya Nambiar: On measurements — for the final commercial decision the execs want a simple one-pager showing delta vs in-house: cost savings, latency improvements, and ops overhead. Can Redwood produce that?
[06:10] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll produce an executive readout with the key levers: batching/caching/quantization and estimated annualized savings.
[06:16] James Park: Also attach the sample 5k prompts and the error breakdown.
[06:20] Diego Alvarez: Will do.
[06:23] [12:00] — (mid-call deep dive) Diego explains kernel selection and quant tradeoffs — somewhat technical, some crosstalk.
[12:49] Diego Alvarez: ...we swapped to tiled attention kernels because the short-sequence codepath uses fewer memory transfers; that's where we got the percentile wins. The quant profile we used is non-uniform 4-bit, not naive symmetric q, so some proper retuning was needed.
[13:05] Priya Nambiar: Was there any impact on memory footprint on the dedicated machines?
[13:09] Diego Alvarez: Down about 30% so you can fit more inference workers per GPU.
[13:15] Ethan Cole: One more ops question — how heavy is the observability agent? We can't have a big sidecar on our prod nodes.
[13:22] Maya Chen: The Redwood telemetry can be configured — lightweight agent or remote push to your logging endpoint. Metrics are low-cardinality by default.
[13:31] Rita Singh: Quick commercial ask — can we get an initial 3-month reserved pilot rather than committing 12 months? It helps ring-fence budget.
[13:38] Maya Chen: We can propose a 3-month pilot reservation with conversion credit toward 12 months if you convert. I'll include both options in the SOW.
[13:46] Priya Nambiar: That would be helpful.
[13:48] James Park: Any blockers?
[13:51] Priya Nambiar: From my side, need the date normalization patch in the final run, Qs answered in the security questionnaire, and the SOW to match the pilot term.
[13:59] Maya Chen: We'll take those. Diego will run the bench, I will send SOW, security pack will be completed.
[14:05] Ethan Cole: Timeline-wise — once we have the SOW and benchmarks in the next week, procurement can potentially sign by 10/24.
[14:12] Rita Singh: That matches my calendar.
[14:15] Maya Chen: Great. Any last questions?
[14:19] Priya Nambiar: No, thanks everyone. Good job to the Redwood team.
[14:23] Diego Alvarez: Thanks.
[14:25] Maya Chen: We'll follow up with action items. End of call.
